note: Stolerman neurodevelopmental syndrome (KDM6B) overlaps with other chromatinopathies like Kabuki syndrome but lacks their hallmark dysmorphisms such as prominent lower eyelid eversion or characteristic distal skeletal/postural findings.

evidence.text: Variants in KDM6B lead to developmental delay, intellectual disability, and dysmorphic features, and are compared to overlapping chromatin-modifier disorders such as Kabuki syndrome 2 (caused by KDM6A).

source.title: Genetic variants in the KDM6B gene are associated with neurodevelopmental delays and dysmorphic features
source.quote: Kabuki syndrome 2 (OMIM 300867) is associated with alterations in KDM6A. Overlapping
